title: Sun Off, Edges On by Default with Sun Controls in Window Options
description: Every app with a 3D preview (world-3d surface) currently defaults to a visible directional sun light and hidden mesh edges. Flip both defaults (sun off, edges on) across all 3D-preview apps (cad, lowpoly, puzzle, infinite/world, procedural, process, forms/module/procedural, shooting), and add a "Sun" section to each app's window options (WindowMeasure tree) with an enable toggle plus azimuth/elevation/intensity sliders, mirroring lowpoly's existing "Show Edges" toggle pattern. Add a shared WorldSunConfig struct + helpers in framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs (world3d_host module) as the single source of truth, thread environment_json through world3d_scene/world3d_scene_extended, and update the React world-3d-host.tsx defaults accordingly. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/3d-by-default-shouldnt-gentle-valiant.md.
summary:
Flipped both 3D-preview defaults and added sun controls to window options across every app with a world-3d surface.

**Shared foundation** — `framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs` (`world3d_host` module): added `WorldSunConfig` (enabled: false, azimuth: 45, elevation: 35, intensity: 0.85, color: #ffffff), `world3d_environment_json`, `world3d_sun_measures` (Sun WindowMeasure group: enable toggle + azimuth/elevation/intensity sliders), `apply_world3d_sun_action`. Threaded a real `environment_json` param through `world3d_scene_extended`, and gave `world3d_scene` a required `sun: &WorldSunConfig` param (breaking change, no compat shim — updated every call site).

**React** — `framework/renderer/react/components/world-3d-host.tsx`: directional light now only renders when `environment.sun.enabled === true` (was unconditional); edges now default to visible via `showEdges ?? true` (was hidden unless explicitly set).

**Per-plugin wiring** (runtime `sun: WorldSunConfig` field, Sun measures group, `toggleSun`/`setSunAzimuth`/`setSunElevation`/`setSunIntensity` action dispatch, round-trip test asserting sun off + edges on by default):
- lowpoly (also flipped `show_edges` default false→true, replaced `#[derive(Default)]` with a manual impl so Rust-constructed defaults match serde defaults)
- cad (added first `window_measures` override; edges already hardcoded true)
- puzzle (d3 and d5 sub-apps, two `world3d_scene_extended` call sites each)
- procedural (app_3d, two world3d_scene call sites sharing one runtime; added first `window_measures` override)
- process (added first `window_measures` override)
- shooting — extended its existing bespoke `ShootingSun`/measures/actions with an `enabled` flag (default false) instead of duplicating the shared helper, since it already had azimuth/elevation/intensity sliders

**Also fixed compile fallout** from the `world3d_scene` signature change: `framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs` (icon-render synthetic scene) and `forms/module/procedural/rs/lib.rs` (stateless embedded preview, no window chrome) now pass `&WorldSunConfig::default()`.

**Out of scope / no changes needed:**
- `infinite/world/rs/lib.rs` — shared native WGPU rendering widget with no owned document/action model; only flipped its local `show_edges` default (struct init + `unwrap_or`) to match. No sun UI to add (no window chrome, no persisted state).
- `framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs`'s `icon_render_*` headless thumbnail path — explicit per-request lights, unrelated to the interactive-preview sun toggle.

**Verification:** full Rust workspace builds clean (`cargo build --workspace`); all touched crates' test suites pass (lowpoly 35, cad 56, puzzle 159 with one pre-existing unrelated failure confirmed via git-stash diff, infinite_world 25, procedural 32, process 12, shooting 23); React suite passes 94/94 (`bun nx run framework-renderer-react:test`). Visually verified in a live lowpoly dev preview (localhost:6078, pre-existing external server): default scene shows edges and no directional highlight, confirming both default flips render correctly. The new Rust-side "Sun" window-options group wasn't visually re-checked in that same running preview since it requires a WASM plugin rebuild and the server is a long-running external/shared process I avoided restarting — its correctness is instead covered by explicit per-plugin unit tests that call `window_measures(...)` and assert the Sun toggle/sliders are present and round-trip through `toggleSun`.
